basics.description: Deploys Segue (portal + API) and its supporting Postgres, Redis, and background Worker into a single Azure Container Apps environment in this subscription.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: All resources in this deployment are created in this region.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Deployment name prefix
basics.toolTip: Short name used to build every resource name in this deployment (e.g. <prefix>-app, <prefix>-postgres).

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting with a letter.

elements.name: postgresMode
elements.label: Postgres deployment type
elements.toolTip: Managed (default, recommended) creates an Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server — no container, no volume; Azure handles patching and automated daily backups with point-in-time restore. Containerized instead keeps a single-replica Postgres container with Azure Files-backed storage — cheaper, but its data only survives a graceful shutdown; choosing it also adds an hourly scheduled backup job as a compensating control (see 'What Gets Created').

elements.name: postgresPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for Segue's own Postgres database — the 'fhirbridge' role's password when Containerized, or the Flexible Server's administrator password when Managed.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: azurePostgresqlSku
elements.label: Managed Postgres pricing tier
elements.toolTip: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server compute/pricing tier. Only used when Postgres deployment type is Managed.

elements.name: azurePostgresqlStorageMb
elements.label: Managed Postgres storage
elements.toolTip: Storage can only be scaled up later, not down — don't over-provision speculatively. Only used when Postgres deployment type is Managed.

elements.name: jwtSigningKey
elements.toolTip: FHIRBridge.Api's Authentication:SigningKey (HS256) — used to sign access/refresh tokens. At least 32 random characters; treat it like a secret.

elements.name: redisMode
elements.label: Redis deployment type
elements.toolTip: Containerized keeps a single-replica Redis container (custom image with a self-signed TLS cert). Managed creates an Azure Managed Redis cluster instead (classic Azure Cache for Redis is retired and already blocked for new caches in some subscriptions) — no container, no self-signed cert to generate; Azure issues its own CA-trusted certificate.

elements.name: redisPassword
elements.toolTip: Password Redis requires to connect (--requirepass) — defense-in-depth on top of network isolation.

elements.name: redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint
elements.label: Redis TLS certificate thumbprint
elements.toolTip: SHA-1 thumbprint of the self-signed certificate baked into the fhirbridge-redis image you built — run containerization/docker/redis-tls/generate-cert.ps1|sh once before building images, which prints this value (e.g. 8638036B0BE54FADF44EEDBFCD2CEC1A80BBB37F). The app refuses the Redis connection if this doesn't match what Redis actually presents.

elements.name: azureCacheForRedisTier
elements.label: Azure Managed Redis SKU
elements.toolTip: Balanced offers a healthy memory/compute ratio; Memory Optimized suits larger, less compute-intensive workloads. All sizes include SLA/high availability and TLS. Only used when Redis deployment type is Managed.

elements.name: secretsMode
elements.label: Tenant/app secret storage
elements.toolTip: Local database (default) keeps tenant connection secrets and app-level secrets on the local DataProtection-encrypted table — no extra Azure resource, no extra permission needed. Azure Key Vault creates a dedicated RBAC-enabled vault, grants the app's managed identities access to it, and moves secret storage + DataProtection key-ring wrapping there instead. Granting that access needs Owner or User Access Administrator on the resource group — see the tooltip on the deployment's own docs if you only have Contributor.

elements.name: seqMode
elements.label: Centralized log viewing (Seq)
elements.toolTip: None (default) — no Seq container; the app logs to console/Log Analytics only. Seq creates a Seq container with its own public URL (protected by the admin password below) that Api, Gateway, and Worker all send structured logs to, for browsing/searching/monitoring them in one place.

elements.name: seqAdminPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for the Seq web UI (SEQ_FIRSTRUN_ADMINPASSWORD) — the only thing protecting that URL, since no other authentication is configured. Only used when Centralized log viewing is Seq.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: wafMode
elements.label: Web Application Firewall
elements.toolTip: None (default) — Segue is reached directly with no inspection layer in front of it. Front Door WAF creates an Azure Front Door (Standard tier) profile with a managed-rule WAF policy in front of the app — Front Door is both a WAF and a global load balancer in one resource. Recommended since this app processes PHI; most healthcare security reviews ask about this specifically.

elements.name: wafPolicyMode
elements.label: WAF policy mode
elements.toolTip: Prevention (default) actually blocks requests the managed rule set flags. Detection only logs/scores them and blocks nothing — a valid choice if you'd rather watch its findings against your own traffic for a while first, but it provides no real protection until switched to Prevention. Only used when Web Application Firewall above is enabled.

elements.name: storageRedundancy
elements.label: Storage redundancy
elements.toolTip: Applies to the storage account backing Azure Files data (Postgres/Redis/keys/Seq, whichever are containerized) and the Postgres backup container. Zone-redundant synchronously replicates across 3 datacenters in the region, protecting against a single-datacenter outage. Locally-redundant keeps all copies in one datacenter and is only cheaper. Not every Azure region supports zone-redundant storage — switch to Locally-redundant if deployment fails with a SKU/region error.

elements.name: postgresSize
elements.label: Postgres size
elements.toolTip: Containerized Postgres container size. Only used when Postgres deployment type is Containerized.

elements.name: redisSize
elements.label: Redis size
elements.toolTip: Redis's own cache/queue memory needs — separate from the data it persists to its file share. Only used when Redis deployment type is Containerized.

elements.name: fhirbridgeAppSize
elements.label: Segue app size
elements.toolTip: Runs both FHIRBridge.Api and FHIRBridge.Gateway in this one container.

elements.name: workerSize
elements.label: Worker size
elements.toolTip: Background scheduler/pipeline processor — no HTTP endpoint.

elements.name: seqSize
elements.label: Seq size
elements.toolTip: Structured log viewer. Only used when Centralized log viewing is Seq.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Version to install
elements.toolTip: The published version tag to deploy (see the vendor registry's release list for available versions).

options.text: The domain fields below are just a reminder for later — entering one here does NOT configure anything in Azure yet. Azure only assigns each app's domain-verification ID once the app already exists, so a domain can never be activated on the very first deploy. Once this deployment finishes, use the separate Step 2 (custom-domain.bicep) Deploy-to-Azure link to actually activate a domain — it re-asks for the domain and does the real work against the now-existing app.

elements.name: fhirbridgeAppIntendedDomain
elements.label: Segue app domain (optional, informational only)
elements.toolTip: e.g. app.customer.com. Not activated by this deployment - just recorded in the outputs as a reminder to complete Step 2 afterward.

options.text:
This deployment creates resources in the selected resource group only:

• Container Apps — Redis, Segue (Api + Gateway), Worker, plus Postgres too if you chose Containerized (plus a 5th, Seq, if you enabled centralized log viewing)
• 1 Container Apps Environment hosting all of the above
• 1 Log Analytics workspace
• 1 Storage Account with Azure File shares (Redis data, Data Protection keys, Postgres data if Containerized, Seq data if enabled) and zone-redundant replication by default
• If Postgres deployment type is Managed (the default): 1 Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server with automated daily backups
• If Postgres deployment type is Containerized instead: 1 scheduled backup job (hourly pg_dump to a dedicated blob container) as a compensating control, since that path's own data only survives a graceful shutdown otherwise
• If Web Application Firewall is enabled: 1 Azure Front Door (Standard) profile with a WAF policy in front of the Segue app — use the deployment's frontDoorEndpointUrl output afterward, not the app's own default URL, so traffic actually passes through the WAF

Custom domains are optional and activated in a SEPARATE deployment (Step 2 - custom-domain.bicep) after this one finishes — any domain entered on the Network Access step here is just a reminder, not yet active. Postgres and Redis are internal-only by default; Seq (if enabled) gets its own public URL specifically so you can browse to it. Deployment outputs include a resourceManifest used by the cleanup scripts.
Double-check the values on the previous steps, then continue to "Review + create" to see the final parameter summary before anything is actually deployed.
